scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Nobody on? Throw to first.
scenarios.why: The only runner is the batter, and he is running to first base. Throw there.

scenarios.ask: Slow ground ball to you at first base. You are two steps from the bag.
scenarios.big: You're closer. Just step on it.
scenarios.why: You can beat the runner to the bag by yourself. No throw needed. Step on first.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right back to you on the mound.
scenarios.big: Bases loaded? Get the run at home.
scenarios.why: Every runner has to run, so the man on third has to go home. Throw to the catcher and stop the run.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base. You are two steps from the bag.
scenarios.big: He has to run. Step on second.
scenarios.why: The batter is running to first, so the runner has to leave first base. You are already there. Step on the bag.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop. The runner takes off for home.
scenarios.big: Two outs? Take the easy one.
scenarios.why: Let him run. If you get the batter at first for the third out, his run does not count.

scenarios.ask: Slow ground ball to you at third base. You have to run in and grab it.
scenarios.big: Slow ball? Take the sure out.
scenarios.why: The ball took too long to get to you. The runner is already at second. Throw to first.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at first base, right next to the bag.
scenarios.big: Nobody on first? He can stay put.
scenarios.why: The runner on second does not have to run. You can't force him out. Step on first and take the easy out.

scenarios.ask: Line drive! You catch it in the air at shortstop.
scenarios.big: You caught it. That's the out.
scenarios.why: The batter is out as soon as you catch it. There is nobody else to get. Give the ball back to the pitcher.

scenarios.ask: The ball dribbles in front of the plate. You grab it.
scenarios.big: Standing on the out? Take it.
scenarios.why: The runner on third has to run home. Home plate is right under your feet. Step on it.

scenarios.ask: Fly ball to center field. You catch it.
scenarios.big: After the catch, throw to second.
scenarios.why: The runner ran when the ball was hit. Throw to second base so he can't steal the extra base.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base.
scenarios.big: Playing back? Take the out.
scenarios.why: Your team is standing deep, so the run is going to score. That is okay. Get the out at first base.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base. You are three steps from the bag.
scenarios.big: Everybody has to run. Take the closest base.
scenarios.why: Both runners have to run, so any base is an out. Second base is closest. Step on it and the inning is over.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to your right. It pulls you toward first base.
scenarios.big: Go where the ball takes you.
scenarios.why: Second base is behind you now. First base is a force out too. Throw the way you are already moving.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right at you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Get two outs, not one.
scenarios.why: The runner on first has to run. Throw to second to start a double play. Two outs ends the inning.

scenarios.ask: Hard ground ball right at you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Two outs beats one run.
scenarios.why: Throwing home only gets one out. Second base can get two and end the inning.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right at you at third base.
scenarios.big: Look him back, then throw to first.
scenarios.why: He does not have to run, so you can't force him out. Stare at him for one second so he stops. Then throw to first.

scenarios.ask: Fly ball to right field. You catch it and the runner runs home.
scenarios.big: He's going home. Throw home.
scenarios.why: He waited for your catch, then took off. Throw to the catcher and try to beat him to the plate.

scenarios.ask: Fly ball to left field. You catch it.
scenarios.big: Count the outs first.
scenarios.why: There were already two outs. Your catch was the third one. The inning is over, so there is nobody to throw at.

scenarios.ask: Short fly ball to right field. You catch it. The runner is already near second.
scenarios.big: He left early. Throw behind him.
scenarios.why: He has to go back and touch first base. Throw to first before he gets there and he is out too.

scenarios.ask: The batter bunts it down the first base line. You grab it.
scenarios.big: Take the out they give you.
scenarios.why: The runner got a head start on the bunt. Don't chase him. Throw to first for the sure out.

scenarios.ask: The batter bunts up the third base line. You charge in and grab it.
scenarios.big: You left your base. Throw to first.
scenarios.why: You ran off third base to get the ball. The shortstop is running over to cover it. First base is the safe out.

scenarios.ask: The ball gets past you in left field. The runner rounds third and heads home.
scenarios.big: Long throw home? Keep it low.
scenarios.why: Throw low and hard toward the plate. Aim at the third baseman standing in the middle, so he can grab it if the throw is off.

scenarios.ask: The ball is hit to left field. You play right field. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Back up the base.
scenarios.why: Outfielders never stand still. Run in behind second base. If the throw gets past everybody, you are there to stop it.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to center. The throw is going home. You are the pitcher. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Pitchers back up the throw.
scenarios.why: Run behind the catcher and stand way back. If the throw gets past him, you stop it and nobody moves up.

scenarios.ask: You have the ball. The runner is caught in the middle.
scenarios.big: Run him back the way he came.
scenarios.why: Chase him toward second base, not third. Then make one hard throw. The worst thing that happens is he ends up where he started.

scenarios.ask: Pop up over the mound. The umpire yells INFIELD FLY — the batter is out.
scenarios.big: Batter's already out. Just catch it.
scenarios.why: The umpire called him out so you can't drop it on purpose. Now nobody has to run. Catch the ball and hold it.

scenarios.ask: Deep fly ball to center. You catch it. The runner tags up and runs to third.
scenarios.big: He's only going one base. Throw to third.
scenarios.why: He is not going home, so home is the wrong throw. Throw toward third base. The shortstop runs out to help you.

scenarios.ask: The ball rolls into the corner in right field. You are very far from home plate.
scenarios.big: Too far? Hit your relay man.
scenarios.why: You can't throw that far on a line. The second baseman runs out to meet you. Throw to him and he throws the rest of the way.

scenarios.ask: Strike three! But the ball bounces off your glove and rolls away.
scenarios.big: Dropped strike three? He can run.
scenarios.why: If you drop strike three and first base is empty, the batter is allowed to run. Go get the ball and throw to first.

scenarios.ask: The ball pulls you way off of first base. The runner heads for third.
scenarios.big: The pitcher covers first.
scenarios.why: You are too far from the bag to get back in time. The pitcher runs over to cover first on every ball hit your way. Toss it to him, chest high. Forget the runner.

scenarios.ask: Hard ground ball to you at third. The runner on third takes off for home!
scenarios.big: He ran. Get him at the plate.
scenarios.why: He can't stop once he goes. You have the ball and he doesn't. Throw home and take the run away.

scenarios.ask: Hard ground ball to you at third base. The runner on third stays on the bag.
scenarios.big: Second base is empty, so third is not a force.
scenarios.why: Stepping on third does nothing — he does not have to run. The runner on first DOES have to run. Throw to second.

scenarios.ask: Hard ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Playing in? Stop the run.
scenarios.why: Your team moved up close for one reason: to keep him from scoring. Throw home.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to right field. You play shortstop. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Somebody has to cover the bag.
scenarios.why: The second baseman ran out to the grass to take the relay throw. That leaves second base empty. You cover it.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to center field. He rounds third and sprints for home.
scenarios.big: Two outs? Let it rip.
scenarios.why: There is nothing to save the ball for. Throw hard toward the plate on one bounce.

scenarios.ask: Slow ground ball to your right at second base. You run in and grab it.
scenarios.big: Slow ball? Take the closest base.
scenarios.why: You might not beat the batter to first. Everybody has to run, so second base is an out too — and it is much closer.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at third base.
scenarios.big: Only one runner. Get him at first.
scenarios.why: The batter is the only runner, and he is running to first base. Throw across and beat him there.

scenarios.ask: The ball comes right back to you on the mound.
scenarios.big: Easy out. Toss it to first.
scenarios.why: The batter is the only runner. Take your time, turn, and make a good throw to first base.

scenarios.ask: The ball dribbles out in front of the plate. You grab it.
scenarios.big: Grab it and fire to first.
scenarios.why: The batter took off for first base as soon as he hit it. He is the only runner. Throw him out.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in left field. The batter is running to first.
scenarios.big: Throw it in ahead of him.
scenarios.why: He already has first base. Second base is where he wants to go next. Throw to second so he stops at first.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Get the lead runner at second.
scenarios.why: The runner from first is heading to second. He is the lead runner. Throw to second before he gets there.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at first base, but you are far off the bag.
scenarios.big: Off the bag? Get the lead runner.
scenarios.why: You are too far from first to race the batter there. The lead runner is heading to second. Throw ahead of him.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in center field. The lead runner is rounding second.
scenarios.big: He wants third. Beat him there.
scenarios.why: The lead runner is already past second base. Third base is where he is going. Throw to third and make him stop.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Two runners on? The lead one wants third.
scenarios.why: The runner from second is the lead runner now, and he is heading to third base. Throw ahead of HIM, not the one behind.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball right at you at third base.
scenarios.big: The lead runner is coming to YOU.
scenarios.why: The runner from second is heading right to your base. You do not even need to throw. Step on third and he is out.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base.
scenarios.big: Throw ahead of the lead runner.
scenarios.why: The runner from second is the lead runner, and he is going to third. Second base is behind him now. Throw to third.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in right field. The lead runner is heading for third.
scenarios.big: Throw to third and stop him.
scenarios.why: The lead runner is trying to take third base. Get the ball there first and he has to stop.

scenarios.ask: Base hit to you in left field. The lead runner is rounding third.
scenarios.big: Now home is the base ahead of him.
scenarios.why: The lead runner is past third and running for the plate. Home is the base ahead of him now. Throw it home.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at shortstop.
scenarios.big: Stop the lead runner at the plate.
scenarios.why: With the bases loaded, the lead runner is heading home from third. Throw to the catcher and stop the run.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at third base.
scenarios.big: Home is one throw away. Take it.
scenarios.why: The runner from third is the lead runner and he is almost home. You are close. Make the short throw to the plate.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to you at second base.
scenarios.big: Get the one heading home.
scenarios.why: Every base has a runner, so the lead runner is running home. First base can wait. Throw to the plate.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to the shortstop. You are the pitcher. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Every throw needs a backup.
scenarios.why: The throw is going to first base. Run behind first, way back. If the throw gets away, you are there to save it.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to third. The throw is going to first. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: Back up the throw at first.
scenarios.why: Right field is behind first base. Run in toward the line. If the throw gets past first, you are the one who saves it.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to the shortstop. You play center field. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: No ball? You still have a job.
scenarios.why: The shortstop will throw to second base. Run in behind second. If the ball gets past, you are there to stop it.

scenarios.ask: Ground ball to the third baseman. Where do YOU run?
scenarios.big: His throw needs a place to land.
scenarios.why: The third baseman is going to throw to first base. That is YOUR base. Get to the bag and be ready to catch it.

scenarios.ask: The shortstop calls the ground ball. Where do YOU go?
scenarios.big: Don't chase it. Cover your base.
scenarios.why: Only one player fields the ball, and this time it is not you. Your job is third base. Go stand on your bag.
